topic: Roundtable: Watch Claude Code Agents Work as a Pixel-Art Office

key_points: You're the boss; Claude Code and Copilot CLI are your employees, each with a desk in a walkable pixel-art map
Terminal tabs don't scale past 3 AI agents — the motivating problem behind building a visual office
Real AI CLI processes (Claude Code / Copilot CLI) run in PTYs, bridged over WebSocket, rendered by Phaser 3
Features: walk up and chat with any agent like an NPC, terminal peek-over-the-shoulder, hire/fire agents on the fly, lo-fi office music, full CLI tool, 100% local
Architecture: Express server + node-pty + JSONL watcher, WebSocket bridge to a Phaser 3 web app
Roundtable MCP server orchestrates Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini and Codex from one UI
Positioning as an 'MCP roundtable' for cross-tool multi-agent orchestration
Differentiates by aggregating multiple agent CLIs through a single Model Context Protocol interface
Real-time visualization of Claude Code agent orchestration
Shows how observability/visualization is the core value-add for multi-agent workflows
Trend of turning opaque agent processes into visible, inspectable flows
Visual multi-agent orchestration for Claude Code
Confirms the trend: developers want a visual layer over multiple Claude Code agents
Stream your terminal, watch AI agents work — 'like Twitch, for shells'
Popularizes the entertainment/spectator angle of watching agents work in real time

stats.fact: AIOffice (pixel-art office for Claude Code + Copilot CLI agents) had ~25 GitHub stars and 4 forks at the time of review.
The motivating problem: terminal tabs don't scale past ~3 concurrent AI coding agents, driving demand for visual multi-agent management.
A wave of visual multi-agent orchestration tools emerged in 2026: AIOffice, agent-flow, rondoflow, claude-colony, dream-team, vibe-claude.
Cross-tool orchestration is a distinct trend: Roundtable MCP aggregates Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini and Codex under one interface.
AIOffice architecture: Express server managing PTY processes for each agent CLI, a JSONL output watcher, WebSocket bridge, and a Phaser 3 web app rendering the pixel-art scene.
The spectator angle is growing: tools like Twitch-terminal let users watch AI agents work in real time, like streaming a shell session.

angles: Gamification of agent management — turning CI/CD and parallel coding tasks into a playable, walkable office makes multi-agent work intuitive and fun
Observability through visualization — the core innovation is making opaque agent work visible and inspectable at a glance
The scaling ceiling of terminal tabs — why parallel agents exceed text-based UIs and need spatial/visual coordination
Local-first, privacy-safe orchestration — 100% local operation using your existing CLI auth, no cloud telemetry
From 'employees you micromanage' to 'peek over the shoulder' — a new mental model for human-in-the-loop agent supervision
